milky_way.name: The Milky Way
milky_way.description: Our home galaxy — a vast, rotating disk of stars, gas, and dust bound together by gravity and dark matter, with a dense central bulge and sweeping spiral arms.

features.name: Galactic Center
features.description: The dense core of the Milky Way, home to a supermassive black hole and a crowded field of stars.

features.name: Spiral Arms
features.description: Sweeping regions of enhanced star formation, including the Perseus, Sagittarius, and Orion arms.

features.name: Stellar Populations
features.description: Older, redder stars concentrated toward the bulge and halo; younger, bluer stars in the spiral arms.

features.name: Dark Matter Halo
features.description: An invisible, massive halo inferred from its gravitational effects, thought to make up most of the galaxy's mass.

features.name: Sagittarius A*
features.description: The supermassive black hole at the galactic center, with a mass of roughly 4 million Suns.

black_hole.name: Sagittarius A*
black_hole.description: The supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way, confirmed through decades of tracking the orbits of stars around an invisible, immensely massive object.

concepts.name: Event Horizon
concepts.description: The boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape its gravity.

concepts.name: Singularity
concepts.description: The theoretical point of infinite density at a black hole's center, where our current physics breaks down.

concepts.name: Accretion Disk
concepts.description: A swirling disk of superheated gas and dust spiraling into a black hole, often glowing brightly before it crosses the event horizon.

concepts.name: Photon Sphere
concepts.description: A region where gravity is strong enough that light can travel in a circular orbit around the black hole.

concepts.name: Gravitational Lensing
concepts.description: The bending of light from background objects as it passes near a black hole's immense gravity.

concepts.name: Time Dilation
concepts.description: Time passes more slowly in strong gravitational fields — an effect predicted by general relativity and confirmed by observation.

black_hole.note: Our Solar System orbits the galactic center from roughly 26,000 light-years away — an immense, safe distance from Sagittarius A*.

scale_journey.label: Human
scale_journey.description: An average human, the starting point of our scale journey.

scale_journey.label: Earth
scale_journey.description: About 7.4 million times taller than a human.

scale_journey.label: Earth–Moon distance
scale_journey.description: The average gap between Earth and its Moon.

scale_journey.label: Solar System (to Neptune)
scale_journey.description: The span from the Sun out to Neptune's orbit.

scale_journey.label: Oort Cloud (theoretical)
scale_journey.description: A theorized shell of icy bodies extending roughly a light-year from the Sun, marking the edge of the Sun's gravitational influence.

scale_journey.label: Distance to Proxima Centauri
scale_journey.description: About 4.24 light-years — the nearest known star system to our Sun.

scale_journey.label: The Milky Way
scale_journey.description: Roughly 100,000 light-years across, containing hundreds of billions of stars.

scale_journey.label: The Local Group
scale_journey.description: A gravitationally bound group of roughly 80 galaxies, including the Milky Way and Andromeda, spanning about 10 million light-years.

scale_journey.label: Observable Universe
scale_journey.description: Roughly 93 billion light-years in diameter, the farthest extent of the universe we can observe.
